claim: WY2026 inflow forecast is 3.27 maf — 34% of the 1991–2020 average.

August 2025 24-Month Study set the WY2026 tier as Mid-Elevation Release Tier with a 7.48 maf standard release.
DOI invoked Section 6.E to reduce annual release to 6.0 maf — unprecedented under the Mid-Elevation Tier.
The May 2026 24-Month Study formally incorporates 1.0 MAF of DROA Flaming Gorge releases as a model input.
The annual tier is locked by the August 24-Month Study; mid-year changes require Section 6.E emergency authority.
The DROA Target Elevation of 3,525 ft provides a 35-ft buffer above minimum power pool (3,490 ft) to allow drought response actions.
2026 DROA Plan calls for 660,000 AF–1 MAF from Flaming Gorge; no anticipated recovery through the plan year.
DROA requires monthly GCD adjustments before upstream CRSP Initial Unit releases.
Approximately 75% of CRSP Basin Fund revenue comes from Glen Canyon Dam hydropower; WAPA marketing obligations are a binding DROA constraint.
CRSP Initial Units have 30.6 maf combined storage capacity; governed by the Law of the River.
The penstocks are incapacitated below 3,490 ft; river outlet works at elevation 3,370 ft (functionally limited at 3,394 ft) were damaged by cavitation in 2023 and are not designed for full-time use.
Reclamation's 3,500 ft operational redline strands 4.4 MAF below it; only 3.7 MAF is accessible with current infrastructure.
Reclamation is assessing three engineering modifications; appraisal study expected late 2026/early 2027; any action requires congressional authorization.
Reclamation cut Lake Powell releases to the legal minimum for the first time; 'reservoir triage' approach usable only once or twice before upstream buffers exhausted.
Approximately 80% of large US reservoirs use medium-to-long range inflow forecasts; western high-elevation systems use snowpack-based long-range horizons.
